answer: Binding each agent identity to a unique hardware secure element that generates per-epoch falcon attestations resists Sybils. Registration requires the device to sign a challenge, proving exclusive control over the chip at the network mesa. An attacker must purchase and provision a separate physical device for every fake identity, since software clones cannot forge atlas-bound attestation roots. This imposes a linear hardware cost that scales directly with the number of Sybils, while honest agents pay only once.
